pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The revenue base is recurring and diversified, which makes debt service predictable. About 95% of revenue is recurring, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, about 75% of sales are made directly, and annual run rate excluding the divested businesses grew 7% to USD 2,412.4 million at 30 June 2026. Management expects churn to remain low, but a retention rate is not disclosed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 65; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C17

Margins and cash conversion are high, and Q3 2026 showed how fast earnings fall when revenue slips. Reported EBITDA margin was 39.61% in FY2025 and 36.77% in the nine months to June 2026, and free cash flow was 0.77x EBITDA over the last twelve months. Part of the FY2025 margin reflects up-front license recognition on longer contracts, because revenue grew 19.18% while annual run rate grew 9.93%. In Q3 2026 revenue fell 6.82% and operating income fell 20.65% because operating expenses stayed flat, a margin loss of about 480 basis points. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C7

Leverage is low and interest cover is wide, so debt service is not the near-term constraint. Net debt was 0.88x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 June 2026 and 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase, against 0.93x at FY2025 and 2.13x at FY2024. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.53x, and would still cover it 16.37x if the July 2026 net borrowing carried the 5.0% rate stated for the credit facility. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C31

The binding constraint is a single maturity window and not the annual cash need. Scheduled principal of USD 1,425.0 million is due almost entirely in fiscal 2028, USD 1,393.7 million or 97.80%, because the revolver and term loan mature on 2028-01-03 and the fixed-rate senior notes in February 2028. The facility becomes a current liability from 2027-01-03, so the refinancing question reaches the balance sheet at 2027-03-31. The notes were quoted at 98.00% of face value on 30 June 2026, which does not by itself signal market stress. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C34; calculation C29

Financial policy is the swing factor and turned against creditors in FY2026. FY2025 repaid USD 553 million of net debt, but repurchases of USD 1,326 million in the nine months to June 2026 and USD 273.7 million in July 2026 were funded in part by net borrowings of USD 225 million and USD 301.3 million. Guided FY2026 repurchases of USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow plus sale cash by USD 251.7 million, so debt or cash on hand must fund the difference. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C28; calculation C26

The March 2026 sale of Kepware and ThingWorx shrank the revenue base and flatters the leverage ratios. Last-twelve-months EBITDA still includes the divested businesses, which produced USD 46 million of revenue in Q3 2025 alone, so leverage on the continuing business is higher than the 0.88x reported, before the July 2026 repurchase lifts net debt to 1.11x pro forma; the issuer guides FY2026 revenue at USD 2,690 million to USD 2,750 million, which is 2% lower to flat on FY2025. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4

Covenant protection cannot be tested, so the view rests on cash flow and not on contractual headroom. The issuer states compliance with all financial and operating covenants at 30 June 2026 without giving the levels, and the facility's commitment fee depends on a total leverage ratio whose definition is not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)

runs.text: The strongest support is cash generation from a recurring, diversified revenue base. About 95% of revenue is recurring, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, and free cash flow of about USD 850 million is guided for FY2026 even after about USD 100 million of divestiture-related cash taxes. Debt principal equals 1.66 years of FY2025 free cash flow, so all of the debt could be repaid from internal cash flow in under two years if repurchases and other uses stopped. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 65; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C9; calculation C25

Low leverage and a large undrawn revolver give creditors room to absorb a weak year. Net debt was 0.88x EBITDA and 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase, cash was USD 351,454 thousand and USD 757.5 million was available to borrow under the revolver at 30 June 2026, before the July 2026 borrowing of USD 301.3 million, and the cash and availability after July 2026 are not established. Cash interest paid was covered 20.53x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C3; calculation C8

The main weakness is a shareholder-return policy that the revolver is now funding. Repurchases of USD 1,326 million in the nine months to June 2026 and USD 273.7 million in July 2026 reversed the net debt repayments of FY2025, and the guided FY2026 repurchases of USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow plus sale cash by USD 251.7 million. The issuer itself states that its credit facility limits could change the amount and timing of repurchases, but the limits are not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C26

Refinancing is concentrated in one window, and part of the debt is exposed to rates. USD 1,393.7 million or 97.80% of scheduled principal falls due in fiscal 2028, and 64.91% of principal is at a variable rate, where each change of 100 basis points costs about USD 9.25 million a year at the June 2026 balances. Revenue timing is lumpy because license revenue is recognised when a contract starts, as the Q3 2026 license decline of 18% on one renewal showed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C6; calculation C30; calculation C16

runs.text: No new debt instrument was issued in the period covered. The 2025 senior notes were redeemed in fiscal 2025 using a revolver draw and cash on hand, which left the 2028 senior notes and the bank facility as the only debt, and the bank facility was amended on 18 November 2025 to remove the asset-sale restriction for the Kepware and ThingWorx sale and to permit other asset sales of up to USD 250 million of book value in a fiscal year. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 102

The sale of Kepware and ThingWorx to Parrot US Buyer, L.P., an entity controlled by TPG-affiliated funds, was agreed on 5 November 2025 for USD 600 million in cash plus contingent consideration of up to USD 125 million, and closed on 13 March 2026 for total consideration of USD 530.8 million, of which USD 523.3 million was received in cash. The dates of the agreement, the closing and the financing events are recorded in the Source readiness events. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; Source readiness (CP-0)

The sale proceeds funded an accelerated repurchase of USD 375 million agreed on 17 March 2026, and a July 2026 repurchase of USD 273.7 million was financed mainly by USD 301.3 million of net credit facility borrowings, so the transaction moved cash from the business to shareholders and, after the proceeds were spent, added to debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction fact pack for Ptc Inc. (issuer id ptc-857005), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the eight supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness output. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is made here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ptc Inc. is a widely held subscription software company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified in the filings, so creditor risk comes from management's capital-allocation policy, which has swung from debt repayment in FY2025 to debt-funded buybacks in FY2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: About 95% of revenue is recurring and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, which supports cash flow, but the March 2026 sale of Kepware and ThingWorx removed part of the revenue base, and the ownership, board and related-party detail held in the proxy statement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The franchise is a single-segment design and product-data software business with broad diversification, which supports debt service. PLM was 62.27% and CAD 37.73% of FY2025 software revenue, the Americas, Europe and Asia Pacific generated 48.45%, 36.33% and 15.22% of FY2025 revenue, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue or receivables, and about 75% of sales are made directly.

The shares are widely held, with a few hundred holders of record at 30 September 2025, and buybacks cut shares outstanding by 7.38% between 30 September 2025 and 30 June 2026; any holder of more than five percent, the board and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's stated policy is to return excess cash to shareholders, and in FY2026 that policy has been funded partly with debt. The sale brought in USD 523.3 million of cash and a USD 375 million accelerated repurchase was funded from the proceeds, open-market repurchases continued, and the July 2026 repurchase of USD 273.7 million was financed mainly by USD 301.3 million of net borrowings. Guided FY2026 repurchases of about USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow plus the sale cash by USD 251.7 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions have been funded from bank debt that was later reduced, which links growth to bank capacity. ServiceMax cost USD 1,448.2 million net of cash in January 2023 and was funded with USD 630 million of revolver and USD 500 million of term loan borrowing, which also repaid the prior facility; pure-systems cost USD 93.5 million in October 2023 and was financed mainly by a revolver draw; the IncQuery purchase of USD 7.9 million in 2025 was small. The March 2026 sale of Kepware and ThingWorx is a disposal of part of the portfolio and not an acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is steady but reported revenue is lumpy. Under the revenue recognition standard the licence portion of an on-premises subscription is recognised when the contract starts, so Q3 2026 licence revenue fell by 18% on a single large renewal of shortened duration while support and cloud revenue held, and about 95% of revenue is recurring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring of results but not of covenants. The annual accounts carry an audit opinion from PricewaterhouseCoopers that the statements present fairly, and the issuer reports ARR, non-GAAP reconciliations and quarterly guidance, but covenant levels, compliance certificates and the credit agreement are not in the sources. Total deferred revenue also fell with the divestiture, by about USD 56 million, which explains part of the fall in the balance since 30 September 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against treating buybacks as a creditor risk is that management repaid debt before the repurchase wave and still holds large undrawn bank capacity: net debt repayments were USD 553 million in FY2025 and USD 757.5 million of the revolver was available to borrow at 30 June 2026. The view would soften if the fourth-quarter FY2026 report shows repurchases slowing to the level of free cash flow, and harden if borrowing keeps funding repurchases beyond the guided total.

fields.value: No new debt instrument was issued in the period covered. The 2025 senior notes were redeemed in fiscal 2025 using a revolver draw and cash on hand, which left the 2028 senior notes and the bank facility as the only debt, and the bank facility was amended on 18 November 2025 to remove the asset-sale restriction for the Kepware and ThingWorx sale and to permit other asset sales of up to USD 250 million of book value in a fiscal year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sale of Kepware and ThingWorx to Parrot US Buyer, L.P., an entity controlled by TPG-affiliated funds, was agreed on 5 November 2025 for USD 600 million in cash plus contingent consideration of up to USD 125 million, and closed on 13 March 2026 for total consideration of USD 530.8 million, of which USD 523.3 million was received in cash. The dates of the agreement, the closing and the financing events are recorded in the Source readiness events.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sale proceeds funded an accelerated repurchase of USD 375 million agreed on 17 March 2026, and a July 2026 repurchase of USD 273.7 million was financed mainly by USD 301.3 million of net credit facility borrowings, so the transaction moved cash from the business to shareholders and, after the proceeds were spent, added to debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by debt-funded repurchases, because they move cash and borrowing capacity to shareholders, which implies higher leverage and a thinner equity cushion; countervailing evidence is the debt repaid in FY2025 and the large undrawn revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Ptc Inc. (issuer id ptc-857005), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the eight supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs. No rating, security recommendation, covenant or recovery conclusion is made here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ptc Inc. has a strong fundamental credit profile, built on recurring software revenue and low leverage, so creditors are well covered today, but the buyback policy and a single fiscal 2028 maturity window are the real risks to that position.

fields.value: The revenue base is recurring and diversified, which makes debt service predictable. About 95% of revenue is recurring, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, about 75% of sales are made directly, and annual run rate excluding the divested businesses grew 7% to USD 2,412.4 million at 30 June 2026. Management expects churn to remain low, but a retention rate is not disclosed.

fields.value: Margins and cash conversion are high, and Q3 2026 showed how fast earnings fall when revenue slips. Reported EBITDA margin was 39.61% in FY2025 and 36.77% in the nine months to June 2026, and free cash flow was 0.77x EBITDA over the last twelve months. Part of the FY2025 margin reflects up-front license recognition on longer contracts, because revenue grew 19.18% while annual run rate grew 9.93%. In Q3 2026 revenue fell 6.82% and operating income fell 20.65% because operating expenses stayed flat, a margin loss of about 480 basis points.

fields.value: The binding constraint is a single maturity window and not the annual cash need. Scheduled principal of USD 1,425.0 million is due almost entirely in fiscal 2028, USD 1,393.7 million or 97.80%, because the revolver and term loan mature on 2028-01-03 and the fixed-rate senior notes in February 2028. The facility becomes a current liability from 2027-01-03, so the refinancing question reaches the balance sheet at 2027-03-31. The notes were quoted at 98.00% of face value on 30 June 2026, which does not by itself signal market stress.

fields.value: The March 2026 sale of Kepware and ThingWorx shrank the revenue base and flatters the leverage ratios. Last-twelve-months EBITDA still includes the divested businesses, which produced USD 46 million of revenue in Q3 2025 alone, so leverage on the continuing business is higher than the 0.88x reported, before the July 2026 repurchase lifts net debt to 1.11x pro forma; the issuer guides FY2026 revenue at USD 2,690 million to USD 2,750 million, which is 2% lower to flat on FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant protection cannot be tested, so the view rests on cash flow and not on contractual headroom. The issuer states compliance with all financial and operating covenants at 30 June 2026 without giving the levels, and the facility's commitment fee depends on a total leverage ratio whose definition is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a positive view concerns policy, not performance. Management showed within nine months that it will add debt to buy back stock: the Q3 2026 repurchase of USD 525 million was more than twice the quarter's earlier target, and the July 2026 repurchase was financed mainly by new borrowing. If that continued until the revolver was used up, total debt would reach 1.79x last-twelve-months EBITDA on the amounts stated at 30 June 2026, and a repeat of the Q3 2026 revenue shortfall would raise the ratio further because operating expenses did not flex. Operating expenses were also held flat partly by transition services income, which the issuer provides for up to 12 months from the sale.

fields.value: The strongest support is cash generation from a recurring, diversified revenue base. About 95% of revenue is recurring, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, and free cash flow of about USD 850 million is guided for FY2026 even after about USD 100 million of divestiture-related cash taxes. Debt principal equals 1.66 years of FY2025 free cash flow, so all of the debt could be repaid from internal cash flow in under two years if repurchases and other uses stopped.

fields.value: The main weakness is a shareholder-return policy that the revolver is now funding. Repurchases of USD 1,326 million in the nine months to June 2026 and USD 273.7 million in July 2026 reversed the net debt repayments of FY2025, and the guided FY2026 repurchases of USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow plus sale cash by USD 251.7 million. fields.value: Refinancing is concentrated in one window, and part of the debt is exposed to rates. USD 1,393.7 million or 97.80% of scheduled principal falls due in fiscal 2028, and 64.91% of principal is at a variable rate, where each change of 100 basis points costs about USD 9.25 million a year at the June 2026 balances. Revenue timing is lumpy because license revenue is recognised when a contract starts, as the Q3 2026 license decline of 18% on one renewal showed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ptc Inc. sells design and product lifecycle software to manufacturers through one reportable segment, and the subscription model supports cash-flow visibility and debt service. Product lifecycle management was 62.27% and computer-aided design 37.73% of FY2025 software revenue, and the Americas, Europe and Asia Pacific produced 48.45%, 36.33% and 15.22% of FY2025 revenue, so the business is spread across two product groups and three regions, although lifecycle management is the larger group. End markets are industrials, aerospace and defense, electronics, automotive and medical technology.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The customer base is tied to discrete manufacturing, which the issuer describes as exposed to import tariffs, high interest rates, volatile exchange rates and supply chain disruption. This is the main cyclical channel into revenue, and the issuer says customers may respond by delaying or reducing purchases, reducing the number of subscriptions or delaying payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership offers no sponsor-extraction channel, but control rights are not established. The company is widely held with a single class of common stock, no sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified in the filings, and the board and larger holders are described only in a proxy statement that is not supplied. Ptc Inc. is the issuer of the 2028 senior notes and the main borrower under the credit facility, and no subsidiary guarantor existed when the FY2025 annual report was filed, so lenders rely on the parent and on security for foreign-subsidiary borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The buyer of Kepware and ThingWorx may owe further consideration of up to USD 125 million after a later sale of those businesses, which is an upside to cash that the issuer has not recognised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is predictable in its recurring part and lumpy in its license part. Support and cloud services were 53.63% of FY2025 revenue and are recognised over the contract term, while license revenue was 42.45% and is recognised when a contract starts, so it moves with contract timing: it grew 44.10% in FY2025 on larger and notably longer contracts and fell 18% in Q3 2026 on one renewal of shortened duration. Revenue grew 19.18% in FY2025, against annual run rate growth of 9.93%, and 11.64% in the nine months to June 2026, and the issuer cites commercial optimisation as a driver, but a price against volume split is not disclosed, so pricing power is not established.

fields.value: Margins are high and carry operating leverage in both directions. Gross margin was 83.76% of revenue in FY2025 and 83.45% in the nine months to June 2026, EBITDA margin was 39.61% and 36.77%, and operating expenses did not fall when Q3 2026 revenue fell, so operating income fell 20.65% on a 6.82% revenue decline. fields.value: Cost flexibility appears limited in the short run. General and administrative expense rose 37.03% in the nine months to June 2026, mainly because acquisition and transaction costs rose from USD 2.4 million to USD 40.0 million, and Q3 2026 operating expenses were held flat partly by transition services income, which the issuer provides for up to 12 months from the sale. The share of fixed cost in the base is not disclosed, so the cost the issuer could remove in a downturn is not established.

fields.value: Capital intensity is very low, so EBITDA turns into free cash flow at a high rate. Additions to property and equipment were 0.40% of FY2025 revenue and 0.79% in the nine months to June 2026, and free cash flow was 1.06x EBITDA in FY2024, 0.79x in FY2025 and 0.77x over the last twelve months. The issuer links a USD 179 million rise in long-term receivables in FY2025 to larger, longer contracts, which is one reason cash conversion fell. Capital expenditure offers little flexibility to protect cash because there is little to cut; the flexible uses of cash are repurchases and acquisitions.

fields.value: Competitive rivalry is the force the filings document best. The issuer names Autodesk, Dassault Systèmes SA and Siemens AG as its main competitors in design and product lifecycle software, and it lists customers adopting competing solutions among its risks; switching costs and market shares are not quantified in the filings, so the strength of the moat is not established. Buyer power is limited by the absence of any customer above 10% of revenue, and the reseller channel is a minority of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic and trade conditions are the macro factors that alter credit quality, through manufacturing demand, rates and currency, while political and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the sources supplied. Technology matters through the issuer's risk language on customers adopting competing solutions or being slow to adopt its artificial intelligence features. The risk language also names high interest rates and tightening credit as reasons for customers to delay purchases.

fields.value: The financial profile is strong and the trend is stable to slightly weaker. The main supports are recurring revenue, EBITDA margin of 36.77% in the nine months to June 2026, free cash flow of 0.77x EBITDA and net debt of 0.88x EBITDA, or 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase; the constraints are the debt-funded repurchases, the fiscal 2028 concentration and the loss of the divested businesses. Lease obligations of USD 184,379 thousand sit outside the debt figure. The datapoints that would allow a firmer view are covenant levels, the balance sheet after July 2026, a retention rate and any issuer rating, none of which is supplied.

fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwind is growth in annual run rate, which the issuer guides at 9% to 9.5% in constant currency excluding divested businesses, and the headwinds are the removal of the sold businesses from revenue, the end of transition services income and rising interest cost on the July 2026 borrowing. Guided FY2026 free cash flow of about USD 850 million is about 1% lower than FY2025 and the issuer expects churn to stay low, which supports repayment capacity but not growth in it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the central credit event is the 2028 refinancing. Replacing the 2028 notes at the 5.0% rate stated for the facility would add about USD 5.0 million a year of interest, which is small against EBITDA, so the refinancing is a question of market access and policy and not of affordability, provided the debt has not been raised by repurchases before then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with tariff-driven weakness among manufacturing customers, who delay purchases and shorten renewals. License revenue, which is recognised when a contract starts, falls first, as it did in Q3 2026 when revenue fell 6.82% and operating income fell 20.65% because operating expenses did not flex. Free cash flow then weakens, annual billing in advance means less cash is collected from smaller contract values, and if repurchases continue beyond free cash flow the revolver supplies the difference; drawing all of the amount available to borrow would take total debt to 1.79x EBITDA on the June 2026 amounts. Management can stop repurchases, which are discretionary, and capital expenditure is small, so resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless repurchases continue into the 2027 refinancing window.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Ptc Inc. presents a strong business profile supported by recurring subscription revenue, high margins and low leverage, but credit quality is constrained by debt-funded repurchases and a single fiscal 2028 maturity window. Cash-flow durability appears strong because free cash flow was 0.77x EBITDA over the last twelve months and guided FY2026 free cash flow is about USD 850 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether net debt stays near the 0.88x EBITDA of June 2026, or the 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase, until the facility becomes current on 2027-01-03. The primary downside path is repurchases funded by the revolver while revenue timing weakens results. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in software, low leverage is a point of difference, but no peer set is supplied, so the comparison is not established. Further analysis would require the covenant terms, the balance sheet after July 2026 and a rating.
